dates.note: Announced with the arXiv paper of 2023-06-20. The weights were published later on Hugging Face (microsoft/phi-1), but no Microsoft page states the day or month.

lifecycle.note: Weights are still downloadable from Microsoft's Hugging Face organisation (checked 2026-10-01).

summary.text: Phi-1 is a 1.3 billion parameter Transformer language model from Microsoft, specialised for basic Python coding and introduced in the paper Textbooks Are All You Need in June 2023. It was trained on textbook-quality web data plus synthetic textbooks and exercises generated with GPT-3.5, and its weights are published on Hugging Face under the MIT License.

changes.text: Adds a new source of synthetic NLP texts to the phi-1 data sources, moving the focus from Python coding to common-sense reasoning in natural language.
The model card lists question-answer, chat and code prompt formats, whereas phi-1 was specialised for basic Python coding.

dates.note: Announced with the arXiv technical report of 2023-09-11, which says the model is open-sourced; no Microsoft page states the day the weights went public on Hugging Face.

lifecycle.note: Weights are still downloadable from Microsoft's Hugging Face organisation (checked 2026-10-01).

relations.note: The report presents phi-1.5 as follow-up work on phi-1 with the same textbook-data approach; the card says it was trained on the phi-1 data sources plus new synthetic NLP texts.

summary.text: Phi-1.5 is a 1.3 billion parameter base language model from Microsoft, presented in a September 2023 technical report that applies the phi-1 textbook-data approach to common-sense reasoning in natural language. Microsoft open-sourced it for research on issues such as hallucination, toxicity and bias, with weights on Hugging Face under the MIT License.

changes.text: Grows from 1.3 billion parameters in Phi-1.5 to 2.7 billion.
Adds new synthetic NLP texts and websites filtered for safety and educational value to the Phi-1.5 data sources.
Microsoft says embedding the knowledge of Phi-1.5 in the larger model, a scaled knowledge transfer, sped up training convergence.

sources.locator: page date; availability in the Azure AI Studio model catalog

lifecycle.note: Weights are still downloadable from Microsoft's Hugging Face organisation (checked 2026-10-01).

relations.note: Nadella calls Phi 2 a scaled-up version of Phi 1.5; the blog describes embedding Phi-1.5 knowledge in Phi-2.

summary.text: Phi-2 is a 2.7 billion parameter base language model from Microsoft, announced by Satya Nadella at Microsoft Ignite in November 2023 as a scaled-up version of Phi-1.5. Microsoft Research released it on 12 December 2023 in the Azure AI Studio model catalog, and its weights are published on Hugging Face under the MIT License.

access.note: At Build 2024 Phi-3-mini and Phi-3-medium were offered through Azure AI models as a service.

sources.locator: Azure AI's models as a service offering

contextWindowTokens.note: Maximum for every size; each size also has a short-context version (4K for mini and medium, 8K for small).

changes.text: Offered in three sizes, 3.8 billion (mini), 7 billion (small) and 14 billion (medium) parameters, against 2.7 billion for Phi-2.
Context window of up to 128K tokens, compared with 2,048 tokens for Phi-2; each size also has a short-context version.
Released as instruction-tuned models, post-trained with supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization; Phi-2 was a base model.
Trained on a scaled-up version of the phi-2 data, made of heavily filtered public web data and synthetic data; phi-3-mini saw 3.3 trillion tokens.

lifecycle.note: Weights of all three sizes are still downloadable from Microsoft's Hugging Face organisation (checked 2026-10-01). Retired from Microsoft Foundry on 2025-08-30 (see milestones).

relations.note: The technical report calls phi-2 its previous model and says the Phi-3 training data is a scaled-up version of the phi-2 data.

summary.text: Phi-3 is a family of instruction-tuned small language models from Microsoft in three sizes: Phi-3-mini (3.8 billion parameters), released on 23 April 2024, and Phi-3-small (7 billion) and Phi-3-medium (14 billion), released at Microsoft Build on 21 May 2024. Each size offers up to 128K tokens of context; weights are on Hugging Face, and mini and medium were also hosted in Azure.

variants.name: Phi-3-mini
variants.note: Offered in 4K and 128K context-length versions. Microsoft published a same-name update of the Phi-3-mini weights in June 2024 (model card release notes); it is not a separate record.

changes.text: Adds image input to the Phi-3-mini language model through an image encoder, connector and projector, keeping a 128K-token context.

lifecycle.note: Weights are still downloadable from Microsoft's Hugging Face organisation (checked 2026-10-01).

relations.note: Built from the Phi-3-mini language model (variant mini of microsoft.phi-3) combined with an image encoder, connector and projector.

summary.text: Phi-3-vision is a 4.2 billion parameter multimodal model from Microsoft that accepts text and images and returns text, the first multimodal model in the Phi-3 family. Introduced at Microsoft Build on 21 May 2024, it builds on Phi-3-mini, was optimised for chart and diagram understanding, and has open weights on Hugging Face under the MIT License.

access.note: The api value rests on the Phi-3.5-mini serverless endpoint in Azure AI Studio.

sources.locator: More Predictable Outputs: Phi-3.5-mini serverless endpoint in Azure AI Studio

changes.text: Adds multilingual support: the Phi-3.5-mini card lists 23 languages, and Microsoft says Phi-3.5-MoE supports more than 20.
Adds a mixture-of-experts model, Phi-3.5-MoE, with 16 experts of 3.8 billion parameters each; 6.6 billion of its 42 billion parameters are active.
Phi-3.5-mini comes only in a 128K-token version, where Phi-3-mini also had a 4K version; the report describes LongRoPE to extend the context.
Phi-3.5-mini adds continued pre-training on multilingual synthetic and filtered data, and proximal policy optimization in post-training.

sources.locator: page date; Today, we are proud to announce

lifecycle.note: Weights of both variants are still downloadable from Microsoft's Hugging Face organisation (checked 2026-10-01). Retired from Microsoft Foundry on 2025-08-30 (see milestones).

summary.text: Phi-3.5 is a Microsoft release of two open-weight text models announced on 22 August 2024: Phi-3.5-mini (3.8 billion parameters) and the mixture-of-experts Phi-3.5-MoE (42 billion in total, 6.6 billion active). Both support multiple languages and 128K tokens of context; Phi-3.5-mini was also offered on a serverless endpoint in Azure AI Studio.

variants.name: Phi-3.5-MoE
variants.note: Mixture-of-experts model; Microsoft called it a new member of the Phi family.

lifecycle.note: Weights are still downloadable from Microsoft's Hugging Face organisation (checked 2026-10-01). Retired from Microsoft Foundry on 2025-08-30 (see milestones).

relations.note: Editorial link along the vision line: the post says Phi-3.5-vision adds multi-frame understanding and improves single-image results, without naming Phi-3-vision as its predecessor.

summary.text: Phi-3.5-vision is a 4.2 billion parameter multimodal model from Microsoft that takes text and images and returns text, announced on 22 August 2024 with Phi-3.5-mini and Phi-3.5-MoE. It adds multi-frame input for comparing images and summarising image sets and video clips, and its weights are on Hugging Face under the MIT License.

access.note: The api value stands for the Azure AI Foundry offering named in the announcement.

changes.text: Training data extends the Phi-3 data with new synthetic textbook-like data and acquired academic books and Q&A datasets; synthetic data is used throughout.
Context length is 16K tokens, compared with 128K tokens for the Phi-3.5 models.
Aimed at complex reasoning such as math; the report credits data quality, the training curriculum and post-training rather than architecture changes.

relations.note: Editorial link along the core Phi line: the post calls Phi-4 the latest member of the Phi family and the report describes minimal changes to the phi-3 architecture, without naming a direct predecessor; Phi-3.5 was the most recent core text release before it.

summary.text: Phi-4 is a 14 billion parameter small language model from Microsoft, released on 12 December 2024 and aimed at complex reasoning such as math as well as conventional language tasks. Microsoft offers it on Azure AI Foundry and as open weights on Hugging Face under the MIT License; its report describes a training recipe centred on data quality, with synthetic data used throughout.

It was offered in Azure AI Foundry, the NVIDIA API Catalog and as MIT-licensed open weights on Hugging Face, and supports function calling, 23 languages and a 128K-token context.

access.note: At launch: Azure AI Foundry (api), Hugging Face (open-weights-download) and the NVIDIA API Catalog (cloud-partner).

Processes text, vision and speech in a single model with a mixture of LoRAs, without separate pipelines per modality.

summary.text: Phi-4-multimodal is a 5.6-billion-parameter model in Microsoft's Phi family that accepts text, image and audio input and produces text, released on 26 February 2025 with Phi-4-mini. It handles all three modalities in one model through a mixture of LoRAs on a Phi-4-mini backbone, and was offered in Azure AI Foundry, the NVIDIA API Catalog and as MIT-licensed open weights.

summary.text: MAI-DS-R1 is an open-weights reasoning model released by Microsoft on 17 April 2025: a version of DeepSeek-R1 that the Microsoft AI team post-trained to answer topics the original blocked and to improve its risk profile. The weights are on Hugging Face under the MIT licence; the hosted API on Azure AI Foundry was retired on 27 February 2026.

summary.text: Phi-4-mini-reasoning is a 3.8-billion-parameter open-weight model from Microsoft for step-by-step math reasoning, released on 30 April 2025 on Azure AI Foundry and Hugging Face under the MIT licence. Built on Phi-4-mini with a 128K-token context, it is aimed at settings with limited compute or latency, such as education, embedded tutoring and edge or mobile devices.

access.note: Azure AI Foundry (api) and Hugging Face (open-weights-download) at release; ONNX-optimized versions for Snapdragon-powered Copilot+ PC NPUs followed on May 15, 2025 (on-device).

outputModalities.note: Responses consist of a chain-of-thought block followed by a summarization block.

changes.text: Fine-tuned to write out a chain of thought before giving a summarized answer.
Maximum length raised from 16K to 32K tokens to fit longer reasoning traces.
Supervised fine-tuning on about 1.4 million prompt-response pairs in math, coding and safety, with reasoning demonstrations generated by OpenAI o3-mini.

lifecycle.note: Weights remain downloadable from Microsoft's Hugging Face organisation; Microsoft Foundry lists Phi-4-reasoning as GA without a retirement date (checked 2026-10-01).

summary.text: Phi-4-reasoning is a 14-billion-parameter open-weight reasoning model from Microsoft, created by supervised fine-tuning of Phi-4 and released on 30 April 2025 on Azure AI Foundry and Hugging Face under the MIT licence. Its answers contain a chain-of-thought section followed by a summary; the Phi-4-reasoning-plus variant adds a short reinforcement learning phase.

variants.name: Phi-4-reasoning-plus
variants.note: Announced with Phi-4-reasoning. Microsoft trained it further with a short phase of outcome-based reinforcement learning; it generates on average about 1.5 times as many tokens as Phi-4-reasoning. Same 14B base and 32k context. Not listed in the Microsoft Foundry retirement schedule; weights on Hugging Face.

changes.text: Compressed to 7.6B total and 2.4B active parameters, from 41.9B total and 6.6B active in Phi-3.5-MoE.
Experts slimmed with the SlimMoE compression framework, with knowledge transferred through staged distillation.

relations.note: Compressed from Phi-3.5-MoE (an inline variant of the Phi-3.5 record) with the SlimMoE method of expert slimming and staged distillation, then post-trained with supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization. The model card says the starting point is the base model shared by Phi-3.5-MoE and GRIN-MoE.

summary.text: Phi-mini-MoE is an open-weights mixture-of-experts language model from Microsoft with 7.6 billion total and 2.4 billion active parameters, compressed from Phi-3.5-MoE with the SlimMoE method and published on Hugging Face in June 2025 under the MIT licence. It handles English text with a 4k-token context; the smaller Phi-tiny-MoE was released with it.

variants.name: Phi-tiny-MoE
variants.note: Smaller model of the same SlimMoE release; the paper presents both as compressed versions of Phi-3.5-MoE. Same 4k context.

changes.text: Replaces the dense Transformer with the SambaY decoder-hybrid-decoder architecture, which uses Gated Memory Units.
Microsoft says it decodes with higher throughput and lower latency than Phi-4-mini-reasoning, especially on long generations.
Context length of 64K tokens, down from 128K for Phi-4-mini-reasoning.
Reasoning training ran without a reinforcement learning stage, according to Microsoft's paper.

summary.text: Phi-4-mini-flash-reasoning is a 3.8-billion-parameter open model from Microsoft for math reasoning with a 64K-token context, released on 9 July 2025 on Azure AI Foundry, the NVIDIA API Catalog and Hugging Face. It uses the SambaY decoder-hybrid-decoder architecture, which combines Mamba state space layers, sliding window attention and Gated Memory Units, and targets edge and mobile use.

access.note: API access for trusted testers on application. Public testing ran on the third-party evaluation platform LMArena; a rollout for certain text use cases in Copilot was announced as planned over the following weeks.

parameters.note: Not disclosed by Microsoft; the announcement describes an in-house mixture-of-experts model pre-trained and post-trained on about 15,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs.

summary.text: MAI-1-preview is a mixture-of-experts language model that Microsoft AI calls its first foundation model trained end to end in-house, announced on 28 August 2025. It was offered for public testing on LMArena and to trusted testers through an API, and Microsoft AI positions it for following instructions and answering everyday consumer queries.

It feeds images into the Phi-4-reasoning language backbone through a SigLIP-2 vision encoder and can either reason step by step or answer directly.

It is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 35 billion active and about 1 trillion total parameters, which Microsoft says it pre-trained from scratch without distillation from third-party models.

description.text: Microsoft, founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen and based in Redmond, Washington, describes itself as a technology company that builds AI-powered platforms and tools. Microsoft Research developed the Phi small language models, released as open models under the MIT License, and the Microsoft AI organization, formed in 2024, develops the MAI model family.
